In [[mathematics]], specifically the field of [[algebra]], '''Sklyanin algebras''' are a class of [[Commutative property|noncommutative]] [[Algebraic structure|algebra]] named after [[Evgeny Sklyanin]]. This class of algebras was first studied in the classification of Artin-Schelter regular<ref name=":3" /> algebras of [[global dimension]] 3 in the 1980s.<ref name=":4">{{cite arXiv|last=Rogalski|first=D.|date=2014-03-12|title=An introduction to Noncommutative Projective Geometry|class=math.RA|eprint=1403.3065}}</ref> Sklyanin algebras can be grouped into two different types, the '''non-degenerate''' Sklyanin algebras and the '''degenerate''' Sklyanin algebras, which have very different properties. A need to understand the non-degenerate Sklyanin algebras better has led to the development of the study of point modules in [[noncommutative geometry]].<ref name=":4" />

== Formal definition ==
Let <math>k</math> be a [[Field (mathematics)|field]] with a [[Root of unity#General definition|primitive cube root of unity]]. Let <math>\mathfrak{D}</math> be the following subset of the [[projective plane]] <math>\textbf{P}_k^2</math>:

<math>\mathfrak{D} = \{ [1:0:0], [0:1:0], [0:0:1] \} \sqcup \{ [a:b:c ] \big| a^3=b^3=c^3\}.</math>

Each point <math>[a:b:c] \in \textbf{P}_k^2</math> gives rise to a (quadratic 3-dimensional) Sklyanin algebra,

<math>S_{a,b,c} = k \langle x,y,z \rangle / (f_1, f_2, f_3),</math>

where,

<math>f_1 = ayz + bzy + cx^2, \quad f_2 = azx + bxz + cy^2, \quad f_3 = axy + b yx + cz^2.</math>

Whenever <math>[a:b:c ] \in \mathfrak{D}</math> we call <math>S_{a,b,c}</math> a '''degenerate Sklyanin algebra''' and whenever <math>[a:b:c] \in \textbf{P}^2 \setminus \mathfrak{D}</math> we say the algebra is '''non-degenerate.'''<ref name=":0">{{cite journal|last=Smith|first=S. Paul|date=15 May 2012|title="Degenerate" 3-dimensional Sklyanin algebras are monomial algebras|arxiv=1112.5809|language=en|journal=Journal of Algebra|volume=358|pages=74–86|doi=10.1016/j.jalgebra.2012.01.039|doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Properties ==
The non-degenerate case shares many properties with the [[Commutative property|commutative]] [[polynomial ring]] <math>k[x,y,z]</math>, whereas the degenerate case enjoys almost none of these properties. Generally the non-degenerate Sklyanin algebras are more challenging to understand than their degenerate counterparts.

=== Properties of degenerate Sklyanin algebras ===
Let <math>S_{\text{deg}}</math> be a degenerate Sklyanin algebra.

* <math>S_{\text{deg}}</math> contains non-zero [[zero divisor]]s.<ref name=":1">{{cite journal|last=Walton|first=Chelsea|date=2011-12-23|title=Degenerate Sklyanin algebras and Generalized Twisted Homogeneous Coordinate rings|journal=Journal of Algebra|volume=322|issue=7|pages=2508–2527|doi=10.1016/j.jalgebra.2009.02.024|doi-access=free|arxiv=0812.0609}}</ref>
* The [[Hilbert series and Hilbert polynomial|Hilbert series]] of <math>S_{\text{deg}}</math> is <math>H_{S_{\text{deg}}} = \frac{1+t}{1-2t}</math>.<ref name=":1" />
* Degenerate Sklyanin algebras have infinite [[Gelfand–Kirillov dimension]].<ref name=":1" />
* <math>S_{\text{deg}}</math> is neither left nor right [[Noetherian ring|Noetherian]].<ref name=":1" />
* <math>S_{\text{deg}}</math> is a [[Koszul algebra]].<ref name=":1" />
* Degenerate Sklyanin algebras have infinite [[global dimension]].<ref name=":1" />

=== Properties of non-degenerate Sklyanin algebras ===
Let <math>S</math> be a non-degenerate Sklyanin algebra.

* <math>S</math> contains no non-zero [[zero divisor]]s.<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|last1=Tate|first1=John|author-link2=John Tate (mathematician)|author-link3=Michel Van den Bergh|last2=van den Bergh|first2=Michel|date=1996-01-01|title=Homological properties of Sklyanin algebras|url=https://doi.org/10.1007/s002220050065|journal=Inventiones Mathematicae|language=en|volume=124|issue=1|pages=619–648|doi=10.1007/s002220050065|bibcode=1996InMat.124..619T|s2cid=121438487|issn=1432-1297|url-access=subscription}}</ref>
* The [[Hilbert series and Hilbert polynomial|hilbert series]] of <math>S</math> is <math>H_{S} = \frac{1}{(1-t)^3}</math>.<ref name=":2" />
* Non-degenerate Sklyanin algebras are [[Noetherian ring|Noetherian]].<ref name=":2" />
* <math>S</math> is [[Koszul algebra|Koszul]].<ref name=":2" />
* Non-degenerate Sklyanin algebras are Artin-Schelter <ref name=":3">{{Cite journal|date=1987-11-01|title=Graded algebras of global dimension 3|journal=[[Advances in Mathematics]]|language=en|volume=66|issue=2|pages=171–216|doi=10.1016/0001-8708(87)90034-X|doi-access=free|issn=0001-8708|last1=Artin|first1=Michael|author-link=Michael Artin|last2=Schelter|first2=William F.}}</ref> regular.<ref name=":2" /> Therefore, they have [[global dimension]] 3 and [[Gelfand–Kirillov dimension]] 3.<ref name=":3" />
*There exists a [[Normal element|normal]] [[Center (algebra)|central]] element in every non-degenerate Sklyanin algebra.<ref>{{cite journal|last=De Laet|first=Kevin|date=October 2017|title=On the center of 3-dimensional and 4-dimensional Sklyanin algebras|arxiv=1612.06158|journal=Journal of Algebra|volume=487|pages=244–268|doi=10.1016/j.jalgebra.2017.05.032|doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Examples ==

=== Degenerate Sklyanin algebras ===
The subset <math>\mathfrak{D}</math> consists of 12 points on the [[projective plane]], which give rise to 12 expressions of degenerate Sklyanin algebras. However, some of these are [[Isomorphism|isomorphic]] and there exists a classification of degenerate Sklyanin algebras into two different cases. Let <math>S_{\text{deg}} = S_{a,b,c}</math> be a degenerate Sklyanin algebra.

* If <math>a=b</math> then <math>S_{\text{deg}}</math> is [[Isomorphism|isomorphic]] to <math>k \langle x,y,z \rangle /(x^2,y^2,z^2)</math>, which is the Sklyanin algebra corresponding to the point <math>[0:0:1] \in \mathfrak{D}</math>.
* If <math>a \neq b</math> then <math>S_{\text{deg}}</math> is [[Isomorphism|isomorphic]] to <math>k \langle x,y,z \rangle /(xy,yx,zx)</math>, which is the Sklyanin algebra corresponding to the point <math>[1:0:0] \in \mathfrak{D}</math>.<ref name=":0" />

These two cases are Zhang twists of each other<ref name=":0" /> and therefore have many properties in common.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Zhang|first=J. J.|date=1996|title=Twisted Graded Algebras and Equivalences of Graded Categories|url=https://londmathsoc.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1112/plms/s3-72.2.281|journal=Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society|language=en|volume=s3-72|issue=2|pages=281–311|doi=10.1112/plms/s3-72.2.281|issn=1460-244X|hdl=2027.42/135651|hdl-access=free|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

=== Non-degenerate Sklyanin algebras ===
The [[Commutative property|commutative]] [[polynomial ring]] <math>k[x,y,z]</math> is [[Isomorphism|isomorphic]] to the non-degenerate Sklyanin algebra <math>S_{1,-1,0} = k \langle x,y,z \rangle /( xy-yx, yz-zy, zx- xz)</math> and is therefore an example of a non-degenerate Sklyanin algebra.

== Point modules ==
The study of point modules is a useful tool which can be used much more widely than just for Sklyanin algebras. Point modules are a way of finding [[projective geometry]] in the underlying structure of [[Noncommutative ring|noncommutative graded rings]]. Originally, the study of point modules was applied to show some of the properties of non-degenerate Sklyanin algebras. For example to find their [[Hilbert series and Hilbert polynomial|Hilbert series]] and determine that non-degenerate Sklyanin algebras do not contain [[zero divisor]]s.<ref name=":4" />

=== Non-degenerate Sklyanin algebras ===
Whenever <math>abc \neq 0</math> and <math>\left( \frac{a^3+b^3+c^3}{3abc} \right) ^3 \neq 1</math> in the definition of a non-degenerate Sklyanin algebra <math>S=S_{a,b,c}</math>, the point modules of <math>S</math> are parametrised by an [[elliptic curve]].<ref name=":4" /> If the parameters <math>a,b,c</math> do not satisfy those constraints, the point modules of any non-degenerate Sklyanin algebra are still parametrised by a closed [[projective variety]] on the [[projective plane]].<ref>{{Citation|last1=Artin|first1=Michael|chapter=Some Algebras Associated to Automorphisms of Elliptic Curves|date=2007|chapter-url=https://doi.org/10.1007/978-0-8176-4574-8_3|title=The Grothendieck Festschrift: A Collection of Articles Written in Honor of the 60th Birthday of Alexander Grothendieck|pages=33–85|editor-last=Cartier|editor-first=Pierre|editor-link=Pierre Cartier (mathematician)|series=Progress in Mathematics|place=Boston, MA|publisher=Birkhäuser|language=en|doi=10.1007/978-0-8176-4574-8_3|isbn=978-0-8176-4574-8|access-date=2021-04-28|last2=Tate|first2=John|author-link2=John Tate (mathematician)|last3=Van den Bergh|first3=M.|author-link3=Michel Van den Bergh|editor2-last=Illusie|editor2-first=Luc|editor2-link=Luc Illusie|editor3-last=Katz|editor3-first=Nicholas M.|editor4-last=Laumon|editor4-first=Gérard |editor3-link=Nick Katz |editor4-link=Gérard Laumon|chapter-url-access=subscription}}</ref> If <math>S</math> is a Sklyanin algebra whose point modules are parametrised by an [[elliptic curve]], then there exists an element <math>g \in S</math> which annihilates all point modules i.e. <math>Mg = 0</math> for all point modules <math>M </math> of <math>S</math>.

=== Degenerate Sklyanin algebras ===
The point modules of degenerate Sklyanin algebras are not parametrised by a [[projective variety]].<ref name=":1" />
